text: Interesting question and a brilliant one at that. One of the things that I've noticed during my engagements so far in this industry is that of course the regulators, the statutory regulators, now the governments, they are keen about protecting investors, ensuring that the public interest is not compromised and all that, and they come up with all of the regulatory frameworks to ensure compliance and all of that. Now the question is, can we or should the crypto industry be regulated by governments or should it be self regulated? So far we've seen some interventions from the government trying to regulate cryptocurrency. We've also seen some self regulatory approaches in Africa as well. We've seen some associations trying to regulate the industry themselves, but so far there doesn't seem to be any clear cut approaches. This is what I think. I think that the financial services industry is a dynamic, complex and ever changing one. When you have an ever changing industry with such technology as the blockchain or cryptocurrency that keeps evolving, then you have to be sure that the regulatory approach has to be right. In Africa we've got an emerging space, we've got a lot of adoption coming from the young people in Africa. We've seen a lot of transactions from Nigeria, from South Africa, from Kenya. And the government is wondering how do we come into this space since 2016, you know, so when this technology started deepening, getting deepened in Africa, we've noticed something. We've noticed that the regulators from the bank to the securities and Exchange Commission would keep telling you that we do not understand this technology and we cannot regulate what we don't understand. Now they say that they are researching and they're trying to acquire the necessary knowledge they would need to effectively and efficiently regulate the industry. But hey, guess what, while they are doing all that, a lot of stuff is going on in the space, good, bad and the ugly. And so you wonder how long is it going to take regulators to come in? It's been like four years in Africa where regulators are telling us they are coming in, they are learning the technology, but a lot has happened in four years. The scams are happening, the good investments are also happening, negative and positive. And so this points the answer to the question. The answer is we need a self regulatory approach. This is the reason why, if it takes regulators so long to come into this space, it's because they need to necessarily understand it. Just like my fellow panelists were saying, we need the right knowledge for us to be able to regulate. And this takes time. You want to be sure that you're not coming into stifling innovation, so you want to take some time. And so we can't blame our regulators for wasting so much time, but we should be able to self regulate the industry. Right? And what I'm looking at, what I think is this, in self regulating, the crypto industry, we need to look at the advantages of self regulation. It has been tested and trusted across the world, from Taiwan to Japan to Indonesia, India as well. Self regulation can work. All right. And this is why we need self regulation. We need self regulation because with the industry we are looking at a flexible approach, not a rigid one. Statutory regulators are inherently rigid and that is understandable because of the procedures that are involved, the procedures they must comply with. But how long can we wait for all that? I think that regulators, statutory regulators, and the banks and the securities and exchange exchange markets can work together with industry players and set up a self regulatory mechanism or approach so that we don't keep waiting. And then the system, the ecosystem is building up fast and it needs certain regulatory mechanisms. So I think I can tell you about seven advantages of self regulation. If we self regulate the crypto industry, this is what the regulators will gain. They'll be able to leverage on the industry specialized knowledge. Right? If our statutory regulators say that they need time to regulate, it's of course because the knowledge gap is wide and so you need to cover that knowledge gap. So while waiting to cover all that wasting so much time, why don't you adopt a self regulatory approach that will bring industry players involved in regulation so that the industry players become the frontiers of regulation, not sitting at the back door. One of the problems with leadership in Africa is that leaders like to be seen, they like to show power. And this is not what the 21st century needs because of the Innovation running, you need to allow industry players take the lead, help you self regulate what you don't understand. And then what you do as self, as a regulator is then to set up what I call general standards of compliance and leave all those details, technical details and all that to industry players because one, they've got industry specialized knowledge. Secondly, another advantage of self regulation is industry representation. Industry representation. If you realize that if regulators jump into the field like elephants and lions with all of the regulatory frameworks, at the end of the day, who is going to comply if the people you have targeted don't even understand what is complicated? So you want to be sure. Yes, yes, thank you. Yes. I just quickly want to add that there should be industry representation and there should be some transparency and accountability and self regulatory mechanism and of course there should be coordination and information sharing between the statutory regulator and the self regulators.
